acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Dragons family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Dragon Emperor, T5, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Four-Horizon Hoard Sovereign (Sovereign) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two wind construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: An immense Dragon with a branching antler-like horn crown, wings like storm fronts, localized body-heat shimmer at landing, and hoard metal grown into distinct armor quadrants linked to four horizon pylons.

Signature mechanic: Imperial Circuit: four hoard-metal pylons face the arena horizons beneath the Emperor's storm-front wings. The Claw pylon causes Whelps to establish moving claims; the Wing pylon links Fledgling landing marks; the Crown pylon closes a Drake circuit; and the Hoard pylon lets an Elder Wyrm lay a coin roost. The Emperor branches its antler crown toward one pylon, conducts that lower-form phase, then lands on the central hoard with one body-warm heat shimmer and grows the selected pylon's metal across the matching armor quadrant. Breaking a pylon during the landing permanently removes both command and armor growth. After two breaks, the Emperor alternates ground and sky sides of the arena through the surviving grammar instead of repeating the Elder Wyrm at larger scale.
battlefieldDuty: Command a phased territorial boss arena through four hoard-metal horizon pylons, each transforming the arena into one learned ground, hop, circuit, or roost grammar before the Emperor enters the exposed center.
constructionDimensions: For the wingless T1 Whelp, pressure-tuned construction stays ground-based: feather-fine cheek and flank scale fringes, hollow spinal channels, an aerodynamic tail fin, and pressure dents beneath the chest point along its four-legged ground pounce; no wing, membrane, takeoff, or flight anatomy appears early.

For T2–T5, maturing flight anatomy adds ribbed translucent membrane windows, vane-like horn branches, adjustable wing camber, and inner-knuckle pressure anchors while retaining directional scale fringes, spinal channels, and tail control.
Across all tiers, debris streamers and directional vapor channels expose force direction while a visible still center sits behind the Whelp's loaded shoulder or inside each later turning lane.
counterplay: Follow the selected lower-form tell, disrupt its claims or route, attack the pylon when the Emperor commits to the central landing, and use the opened armor quadrant as shelter from the alternating ground-sky pass; each destroyed pylon permanently simplifies the circuit. Affinity signal: For the wingless T1 Whelp, cheek fringes stream flat before its ground pounce while a still pressure pocket forms behind the loaded shoulder; entering that lee or striking the grounded shoulder spoils the launch. For T2–T5, bowed wing windows and the still inner-knuckle anchor expose the corresponding flight turn.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only wind treatment without tier-appropriate ground-pressure or flight construction and directional debris
Glow-only wind treatment without readable airflow or a stable pressure anchor
Transparency alone that removes scale and horn construction, invents Whelp membranes, or erases later wing membranes
Omnidirectional cloud effects that hide the announced ground-pounce or flight lane
identityInvariants: Long neck and tail, deep chest, four clawed limbs, wedge-shaped horned skull, and wings that emerge and expand after the wingless first form.
Each individual holds one coherent metallic or jewel-tone scale identity with a paler underbelly and bright reflective eyes, rather than changing base identity by affinity.
Overlapping scales, horn, bone spurs, and leathery wing membrane retain reptilian load paths and readable joints at every tier.
Horn crowns, spinal ridges, battle scars, torn membrane, and hoard metal fused into old belly scales accumulate as age and territorial history.
Wingspan and horn crown escalate together from absent wings and horn nubs to storm-front wings and branching imperial antlers, while the ground-to-sky grammar remains recognizable.
telegraph: One antler branch hooks toward a horizon, the matching hoard metal rings through the hide, the vast wings bank like a storm front, and every lower Dragon turns its head, horn, or landing marker toward the selected pylon.
